{
  "plan": "# Restrict Replay Pagination to Command Issuer\n\n## Overview\nCurrently, anyone who sees a replay message can click pagination buttons and navigate through it. This change ensures only the user who issued the &#96;/checkersreplay&#96; command can paginate.\n\n## Implementation Details\n\n### 1. Modify &#96;replay_command&#96; ([handlers.py](handlers.py) lines 377-422)\n- When creating replay buttons, include the command issuer's &#96;user.id&#96; in the callback_data\n- Change format from &#96;replay_{game_id}_0&#96; to &#96;replay_{game_id}_0_{user_id}&#96;\n- This ensures the initial replay view is tied to the command issuer\n\n### 2. Update &#96;replay_game_callback&#96; ([handlers.py](handlers.py) lines 572-662)\n- Parse the user_id from callback_data (handle both old format for backward compatibility and new format)\n- Validate that &#96;query.from_user.id&#96; matches the stored &#96;user_id&#96;\n- If validation fails, show an alert: \"❌ Тільки автор команди може переглядати цей повтор.\"\n- If validation passes or user_id is not present (backward compatibility), proceed with rendering\n- Include the &#96;user_id&#96; in all pagination buttons (⏪ Попередній, ⏩ Наступний, 🔁 На початок, 🏁 Фінал) to maintain the restriction\n\n### 3. Handle Game End Message Replay Button ([handlers.py](handlers.py) line 1442)\n- The replay button in game end messages should allow both players to view the replay\n- For this case, check if the user is one of the game players (&#96;red_player_id&#96; or &#96;white_player_id&#96;)\n- If user is a player, allow pagination; otherwise, restrict it\n- This maintains the existing behavior where both players can review their completed game\n\n## Callback Data Format\n- New format: &#96;replay_{game_id}_{step}_{user_id}&#96;\n- Old format (for backward compatibility): &#96;replay_{game_id}_{step}&#96; (will allow access if user_id not present, but this is only for game end messages)\n\n## Security Flow\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser issues /checkersreplay\n  ↓\nButton created with user_id in callback_data\n  ↓\nUser clicks button → replay_game_callback checks user_id\n  ↓\nIf match: allow pagination, include user_id in all buttons\nIf no match: show alert, deny access\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Testing Considerations\n- Test that only command issuer can paginate\n- Test that other users get denied with alert\n- Test backward compatibility with game end message replay buttons\n- Verify both players can still access replay from game end message",

## Summary of Changes

1. Modified `replay_command` (line 415): Updated the callback_data format from `replay_{game_id}_0` to `replay_{game_id}_0_{user.id}` to include the command issuer's user ID.

2. Updated `replay_game_callback` (lines 585-623):
   - Parses user_id from callback_data, supporting both old and new formats
   - Validates access:
     - New format: only the command issuer (authorized_user_id) can access
     - Old format (backward compatibility): allows access if the user is one of the game players
   - Shows an alert if access is denied

3. Updated pagination buttons (lines 666-683): All pagination buttons (⏪ Попередній, ⏩ Наступний, 🔁 На початок, 🏁 Фінал) now include `authorized_user_id` to maintain access control throughout pagination.

4. Game end message replay button (line 1471): Uses the old format (no user_id), allowing both players to access the replay independently via the backward compatibility logic.

## How It Works

- `/checkersreplay` command: Only the command issuer can paginate through the replay
- Game end message replay: Both players can access and paginate independently
- Other users: Cannot access replays they didn't initiate or aren't part of

The implementation maintains backward compatibility while adding the security restriction for command-initiated replays.
